introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - Ordinary Level Examination. Computer Science (0595), Paper 3 (practical), June 2025. Duration: two and a half hours. Do all the tasks (Task I, Task II, Task III) specified in this question paper.**

The booklet reproduced here contains four versions of the same practical paper, headed Group One, Group Two, Group Three and Group Four (booklets 00/0595/3/Grp 1, Grp 2, Grp 3 and Grp 4). Each version has three tasks: Task I (word processing, 20 marks), Task II (spreadsheet, 20 marks) and Task III (reading and running a short C or Pascal program, 10 marks). A candidate works on one group only.

Enter the information required in the shaded boxes. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. All written answers should be provided in the spaces provided in this question booklet. Calculators are NOT allowed.

The working files named in the tasks (documents, workbooks and pictures supplied in the candidate folder) are supplied on the day; they are not reproduced in the printed paper.
enonce_intro_markdown:
**GROUP ONE - TASK II (20 marks)**

You are provided with a file **inflation worksheet.xls** containing the worksheet below.

![fig-1](gce-ol-computer-science-2025-p3-officiel-cameroun_exercice_G1-T2_fig_1.png)

*Figure: the worksheet. Row 1 holds the headings (SN, Item, Weightage, 2018 Price, 2019 Price, 2019 Inc, 2019 % Inc, 2020 Price, 2020 Inc, 2020 % Inc) in columns A to J; the eight items are in rows 2 to 9; row 10 is Basket Value; a small table in rows 13 to 15 has the years 2019 (column E) and 2020 (column F) in row 13, CPI in row 14 and Inflation Rate in row 15.*

| SN | Item | Weightage | 2018 Price | 2019 Price | 2019 Inc | 2019 % Inc | 2020 Price | 2020 Inc | 2020 % Inc |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Flour | 15% | 400 | 800 | | | 1000 | | |
| 2 | Fuel | 20% | 700 | 550 | | | 1500 | | |
| 3 | Rice | 14% | 200 | 300 | | | 700 | | |
| 4 | Sugar | 30% | 800 | 1000 | | | 1400 | | |
| 5 | Cooking oil | 10% | 900 | 1400 | | | 2000 | | |
| 6 | Tomatoes | 20% | 300 | 500 | | | 900 | | |
| 7 | Education | 20% | 12000 | 8000 | | | 19000 | | |
| 8 | Kerozene | 5% | 300 | 150 | | | 700 | | |
| | Basket Value | | | | | | | | |

| | 2019 | 2020 |
|---|---|---|
| CPI | | |
| Inflation Rate | | |

Refer to the formulae below as you answer the questions that follow.

- Price increase (i.e., 2019 Inc, 2020 Inc) = New price - Old price
- % Price increase (i.e., 2019 % Inc and 2020 % Inc) = Price increase/Old price
- Basket Value for 2018 = SUMPRODUCT(C2:C9, D2:D9)
- CPI for 2019 = Basket Value for 2019/Basket Value for 2018
- Inflation rate for 2020 = (CPI for 2020 - CPI for 2019)/CPI for 2019

figures.legende: Feuille de calcul de l'inflation : prix 2018, 2019 et 2020 de huit produits, pondérations, lignes Basket Value, CPI et Inflation Rate

incertitudes: Le PDF (23 pages, scan avec une couche texte OCR bruitée, relu en image page par page) contient QUATRE versions du même sujet pratique : « Group One » (pages 1 à 6, livret 00/0595/3/Grp 1), « Group Two » (pages 7 à 11, Grp 2), « Group Three » (pages 12 à 17, Grp 3) et « Group Four » (pages 18 à 23, Grp 4). Page de garde vérifiée : GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD, ORDINARY LEVEL EXAMINATION, COMPUTER SCIENCE, 0595, Paper number 3, juin 2025, deux heures et demie. Chaque version a trois tâches : Task I (traitement de texte, 20 points), Task II (tableur, 20 points) et Task III (programme C ou Pascal, 10 points). Transcrites en douze fichiers : numero_exercice G1-T1 à G4-T3 ; groupes ["GROUP 1"] à ["GROUP 4"] ; regles_choix vide : le sujet dit « Do all the tasks » ; le candidat ne passe qu'un seul groupe (non exprimable) et, à la Task III, choisit le programme C ou le programme Pascal (non exprimable non plus).
Les filigranes gcerevision.com / Kawlo, les cadres d'en-tête (numéro de centre, nom du candidat, cadre « For examiners' use only »), les lignes à compléter et les artefacts du scanner sont ignorés.

Aucun logiciel (traitement de texte, tableur) n'a été exécuté : les menus et les étapes sont donnés de mémoire, sous une forme générale, sans citer de version de logiciel, et ne sont pas testés. Les formules de tableur ont été traduites en Python et calculées sur les données du sujet ; les résultats annoncés dans les corrigés en sont recopiés.
Aucun corrigé officiel n'existe : les réponses sont rédigées. Les « marking ideas » sont des répartitions indicatives faites d'après les points imprimés ; le barème du jury n'est pas connu.
Les fichiers de travail du jour (documents, classeurs, images) ne figurent pas dans le PDF : les corrigés donnent la démarche exacte et n'inventent aucune valeur de ces fichiers.

Task II : la feuille est reproduite en figure (page 3 du PDF, extraite sans filigrane par le régime « cuit » et le filtre de niveaux, contrôle OCR OK) et ses valeurs sont aussi recopiées en tableau Markdown. Les pondérations (15 %, 20 %, 14 %, 30 %, 10 %, 20 %, 20 %, 5 %) totalisent 134 % et non 100 % : le sujet est conservé tel quel, SUMPRODUCT n'exige pas que la somme soit 100 %.

Question 2 : la plage imprimée se lit « E14:F1 » (dernier caractère coupé sur le scan) ; elle est lue « E14:F15 », la plage des CPI et du taux d'inflation (E14, F14, F15), ce que confirme le tableau de la figure.

Questions 7 et 8 : le sujet ne donne la formule que pour le CPI de 2019 (panier 2019 / panier 2018, année de base 2018). Le CPI de 2020 est lu par analogie : panier 2020 (H10) / panier 2018 (D10). Le taux d'inflation 2020 est (CPI 2020 - CPI 2019) / CPI 2019, comme imprimé. Résultats recalculés avec Python : D10 = 3033, E10 = 2419,5, H10 = 5183, CPI 2019 = 0,7977, CPI 2020 = 1,7089, inflation = 114,22 %.

Question 9 : le sujet demande les formules de F2, G2, I2, J2, F14 et F15 ; I2 et J2 (hausse 2020 = prix 2020 - prix 2019, puis en % du prix 2019) sont déduits de la définition imprimée « New price - Old price ». La position des libellés CPI et Inflation Rate (colonne D, valeurs en E et F) est lue sur la figure.
Points imprimés : 2 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 4 = 20, comme l'en-tête. Les étapes 1, 10 et 11 (ouvrir, enregistrer, imprimer) n'ont pas de points.

questions.enonce_markdown: Launch your spreadsheet software and open the file. Save as Task 2.
questions.corrige_markdown: Launch the spreadsheet program, *File* > *Open* > **inflation worksheet.xls** (candidate folder), then *File* > *Save As* and save it as **Task 2** before any change. No mark is printed for this step.

questions.enonce_markdown: Apply the percentage format to the cells in the ranges G2:G9 and J2:J9 and E14:F15  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select **G2:G9**, hold **Ctrl** and select **J2:J9**, then still holding Ctrl select **E14:F15**. On the *Home* tab click **Percent Style** (%) (or *Format Cells* > *Number* > *Percentage*). The ranges now display their values as percentages, for example 0.5 as 50%.

*Marking idea (2 marks):* the three ranges selected (1); percentage format applied (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Format Cells D10, E10, and H10 to display numbers with two decimal places  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Select **D10**, **E10** and **H10** (hold Ctrl), then *Home* > *Format Cells* > *Number* > **Number** with **Decimal places: 2** (or use the *Increase Decimal* button twice). Once the formulas of question 6 are entered, the cells display **3033.00**, **2419.50** and **5183.00**.

*Marking idea (2 marks):* the three cells selected (1); two decimal places (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: In Cell F2, enter the formula to compute **2019 Inc** for flour. Copy the formula all the way down to Cell F9.  *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The price increase is the new price minus the old price: for 2019 the new price is in column E and the old price (2018) in column D.

**F2: `=E2-D2`**

Then select F2 and drag the *fill handle* (the small square at its bottom right corner) down to **F9**. The formula adjusts by itself (relative references): F3 is `=E3-D3`, ..., F9 is `=E9-D9`.

Results (recalculated with Python): F2 to F9 = 400, -150, 100, 200, 500, 200, -4000, -150 (Fuel, Education and Kerozene became cheaper).

*Marking idea (3 marks):* formula `E2-D2` with the right order (1); starts with = (1); copied down to F9 (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: In Cell G2, enter the formula to compute **2019 % Inc** for flour. Copy the formula all the way down to Cell G9.  *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The percentage increase is the price increase divided by the old price:

**G2: `=F2/D2`**

Drag the fill handle from G2 down to **G9**. With the percentage format of question 2 the column shows: G2 = 100%, G3 = -21%, G4 = 50%, G5 = 25%, G6 = 56%, G7 = 67%, G8 = -33%, G9 = -50% (exact values 100%, -21.43%, 50%, 25%, 55.56%, 66.67%, -33.33%, -50%, recalculated with Python).

*Marking idea (3 marks):* increase divided by the old price (2018 price, column D) (1); formula correct in G2 (1); copied to G9 (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: In cell D10, E10 and H10, enter the formula to compute the Basket Value for 2018, 2019, and 2020 respectively.  *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The basket value is the sum of the products weightage x price, which is exactly what **SUMPRODUCT** computes on two ranges of the same size. The weightages are in C2:C9 (they are stored as percentages, 15% = 0.15).

- **D10 (2018): `=SUMPRODUCT(C2:C9,D2:D9)`** = 3033.00
- **E10 (2019): `=SUMPRODUCT(C2:C9,E2:E9)`** = 2419.50
- **H10 (2020): `=SUMPRODUCT(C2:C9,H2:H9)`** = 5183.00

Check for 2018: 0.15 x 400 + 0.20 x 700 + 0.14 x 200 + 0.30 x 800 + 0.10 x 900 + 0.20 x 300 + 0.20 x 12000 + 0.05 x 300 = 60 + 140 + 28 + 240 + 90 + 60 + 2400 + 15 = 3033.

*Marking idea (3 marks):* one mark for each of the three cells with the right price column (D, E, H) and the weightage range C2:C9.

questions.enonce_markdown: Compute CPI for 2019 and 2020 in Cells E14 and F14 respectively.  *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The paper defines CPI for 2019 as the basket value of 2019 divided by the basket value of the base year 2018; CPI for 2020 is obtained in the same way with the basket value of 2020.

- **E14: `=E10/D10`** = 0.7977 (displayed 80% with the percentage format)
- **F14: `=H10/D10`** = 1.7089 (displayed 171%)

*Marking idea (2 marks):* E14 correct (1); F14 correct, using H10 and the 2018 basket D10 (1).

questions.enonce_markdown: Compute the 2020 inflation rate in Cell F15  *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Inflation rate for 2020 = (CPI for 2020 - CPI for 2019) / CPI for 2019, with the CPI of 2019 in E14 and the CPI of 2020 in F14.

**F15: `=(F14-E14)/E14`** = 1.1422, displayed **114%** (114.22% before rounding).

Do not forget the brackets: without them, `=F14-E14/E14` divides E14 by itself first (giving 1) and then subtracts the result from F14, which is wrong (0.7089 instead of 1.1422).

*Marking idea (1 mark):* the right formula with the brackets.

| Cell | Formula | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| F2 | `=E2-D2` | 2019 price increase (2019 price - 2018 price) |
| G2 | `=F2/D2` | 2019 % increase (increase / 2018 price) |
| I2 | `=H2-E2` | 2020 price increase (2020 price - 2019 price) |
| J2 | `=I2/E2` | 2020 % increase (increase / 2019 price) |
| F14 | `=H10/D10` | CPI for 2020 (basket 2020 / basket 2018) |
| F15 | `=(F14-E14)/E14` | inflation rate for 2020 |

I2 and J2 are copied down to I9 and J9 for the other items. Values: I2:I9 = 200, 950, 400, 400, 600, 400, 11000, 550 and J2:J9 = 25%, 172.73%, 133.33%, 40%, 42.86%, 80%, 137.5%, 366.67% (recalculated with Python; the percentage format with no decimal shows 25%, 173%, 133%, 40%, 43%, 80%, 138%, 367%).

*Marking idea (4 marks):* F2 and G2 (1); I2 and J2 (1); F14 (1); F15 (1) - indicative split.
